title: You don’t think about it when you wake up.
paragraphs: You don’t think about it when you wake up.
You check your phone. You scroll. You move through your day like time is something you own… like tomorrow is guaranteed.
But then something interrupts you.

A funeral passes by.
A name you recognize shows up in a post.
A quiet moment hits you when the noise dies down.
And for a second… just a second… it whispers:
You’re not staying here forever.
Then you push it away.
Because facing it would change everything.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
There was a moment in the beginning—before your plans, before your ambitions, before your secret sins and private justifications—when God formed man from the ground. Not gold. Not marble. Dust.
“And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” — Genesis 2:7
Dust.
That’s where you started.
And whether you ignore it or not… that’s where you’re going back.
“For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.” — Genesis 3:19
Read that again.

Not might return.
Not eventually, maybe.
Will.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
It’s not just about your body.
You’ve been living like your life is permanent. Like your choices don’t echo beyond today. Like the hidden things don’t matter because no one else sees them.
But God saw it.

That compromise you justified.
That bitterness you held onto.
That moment you knew was wrong—and still did it anyway.
You knew.
You felt that conviction, that quiet tightening in your chest… and you silenced it.
Because it was easier to scroll than to repent.
Easier to laugh than to confront what’s rotting underneath.
And now you’re moving… breathing… functioning…
But spiritually?
Dry.
Like dust already.
There’s a kind of life that looks alive on the outside but is already decaying on the inside. No hunger for God. No fear of sin. No urgency.
Just routine.
Just distraction.
Just delay.
Until one day, the body catches up with the soul.
And everything you avoided becomes unavoidable.
Hebrews 9:27 says, “It is appointed for man to die once, and after that comes judgment.”

No edits.
No rewrites.
No second life to “do better.”
Just truth.
And here’s the tension you feel but don’t want to name:
If you stood before God right now… you wouldn’t be ready.
Not because you’re “trying your best.”
Not because you’ve done some good things.
Because sin hasn’t been dealt with.
And sin doesn’t disappear with time.
It’s carried.
Unless it’s removed.
That’s where everything shifts.
Because the same God who said you would return to dust… stepped into that dust Himself.
Jesus Christ didn’t stay distant from your condition.
He entered it.
He took on flesh. He walked among the broken. He saw the hypocrisy, the hidden sin, the religious masks… and He didn’t ignore it.
He confronted it.
Then He did something no one else could do.
“He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree…” — 1 Peter 2:24
The weight you’re carrying… the guilt you try to outwork… the shame you bury…
He took it.
Not so you could stay the same.
But so you could be made new.
Not dust waiting for judgment—
But a soul redeemed by grace.
“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.” — 2 Corinthians 5:17
That’s the difference between two futures.
One returns to dust having ignored the truth.
The other returns to dust… but rises again in Christ.
Because Jesus didn’t stay in the grave.
And if you belong to Him—you won’t either.
Not because they don’t understand…
But because they do.
And they don’t want to respond.
But something in you is still here.
Still reading.
Still feeling that weight.
That’s not random.
That’s conviction.
So don’t bury it again.
Say it plainly—if this is you:
“I’ve been living like this life is all there is… and I know it’s not.”
Or if you feel it deeper:
“I need Jesus. Not later. Now.”
Follow if you’re done pretending.
This isn’t about fear.
It’s about truth.
You are dust.
But in Christ—
You don’t have to stay that way.
